title: MIPI M-PHY lane: full 8b/10b (256 D-codes, 12 K-codes, running disparity), G1 / G2 bit rates, HIBERN8 with wake burst, and the receiver (comma alignment, decode, code and disparity checks)

fields.desc: write 1: enter HIBERN8 (SAVE state, lines DIF-Z) once the lane is idle; a buffered byte goes first
write 1: leave HIBERN8 (8-clock DIF-N wake burst)
write 1: clear the sticky receive / transmit error (an error in the same clock wins)
0: G1 (1 bit per clock), 1: G2 (1 bit per 2 clocks); change only while the lane is idle (a change while locked makes the receiver re-hunt)

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: Byte to send; start each burst with the comma K28.5 (0xBC with K). A byte every 10 bit times keeps the burst going; a gap ends it

fdesc.tx_k: 1: control code (K28.0-7, K23.7, K27.7, K29.7, K30.7; other K-codes are dropped with ERROR)

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Byte decoded by the receiver (the comma included); reading RX frees it

fields.desc: the receiver found the comma and frames 10-bit words
the receive line is in DIF-Z (hibernated)

irqs.name: ERROR
irqs.desc: an unsupported K-code was dropped, or the receiver saw an invalid code or a disparity error; sticky in the core, so the bit is set again on every clock until CMD.irq_clear

notes: tx_dif_p / tx_dif_n (transmit line) and rx_dif_p / rx_dif_n (receive line) pass through unchanged: DIF-N (0,1) idle or bit 0, DIF-P (1,0) bit 1, DIF-Z (0,0) hibernated.
At G1 a byte takes 10 clocks: TX must be written, and RX read, at that rate (RX holds one byte; a byte arriving with RX full is dropped, RX_OVF).
